transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 78 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (CTO - Novae), Sofia Morales (Lead ML Eng - Novae), Diego Rivera (Platform - Novae)

Summary: (auto) agreed pilot scope, bench plan, and next steps. Some minor transcription glitches below.

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros, and then we'll dig into what success looks like for your team.
[00:12] Raj Patel: Hi, Raj here. We'll, we want a POC that proves we can run our customer support summarization + structured extraction pipeline with production-ish load and reasonable cost. Key for us is being able to validate structured JSON extraction accuracy.
[00:25] Sofia Morales: And hi, Sofia. We'll also want to hit throughput targets — around 40 requests per second sustained during peak windows — that's roughly what our live traffic is.
[00:33] Liam O'Connor: Great, thanks. Quick note on Redwood side: we can do both hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints and our native SDK. SDK gives better batching and KV cache hooks; OpenAI-compatible is easier for fast integration since your current stack uses the OpenAI client.
[00:49] Diego Rivera: Quick question — is the function calling you support the same as OpenAI's? We rely on structured function responses to populate our downstream systems.
[00:57] Liam O'Connor: It's compatible in semantics and we accept the same function schemas, but there are slight differences in streaming and retries. We have guidance in the sample SDK for idempotency and partial responses. We should run a few function-calling benchmarks to ensure reliability under retries and backpressure.
[01:15] Raj Patel: Success metrics: p95 latency below 250ms for 512 tokens, p99 below 450ms, throughput 40 rps sustained, and structured extraction F1 >= 0.92 on our eval set. Also cost target under $0.025 per 1k tokens processed.
[01:33] Maya Chen: That sounds reasonable. For the POC timeline, do you prefer an accelerated 4-week sprint or a more breadth 8-week pilot?
[01:41] Sofia Morales: Given compliance reviews — SOC2 audit, KMS integration — we need time, so 6-8 weeks is safer. We can phase features: week 1-2 integration + small smoke benchmarks, week 3-5 large scale benchmarks and tool-calling stress, week 6 wrap and roll decision.
[02:02] Maya Chen: We'll document a concrete plan. Immediate bench plan: you provide a 7-day anonymized traffic replay and the prompt set, we run a synthetic replay at scaled QPS and also do a live compare against your current provider.
[02:15] Raj Patel: Yep, we'll aim to get that by Tuesday the 15th. Also need to check data residency for EU customers — some tenants require EU-only hosts.
[02:25] Liam O'Connor: We have regional routing and can pin an instance to eu-west. For Private deployment we can do VPC + on-prem if necessary, but that adds setup time. KMS integration for key wrapping is available.
[02:40] Diego Rivera: How are audit logs surfaced? We need immutable logs for requests and token counts.
[02:45] Maya Chen: Console exposes per-token billing traces and request logs; we can also stream logs to your S3 or SIEM. We'll include retention SLAs in the pilot agreement.
[02:58] Sofia Morales: On the integration approach, if we use the OpenAI-compatible endpoints we can swap the base url in our current codebase and get early results. But we lose some advanced controls like prefix caching and certain quantization routes, right?
[03:11] Liam O'Connor: Correct — SDK exposes direct batching controls, KV cache hooks, and optimized kernels for specific sequence patterns; the OpenAI-compatible layer still benefits from our runtime optimizations but with fewer knobs surfaced. For POC I'd recommend starting with OpenAI-compatible for speed, then switch to SDK for the final pilot run where we need cost optimizations.
[03:33] Raj Patel: About function calling reliability — we need guaranteed order of operations when invoking downstream enrichment services, or at least idempotence in retries. Any suggestions?
[03:42] Liam O'Connor: We recommend using idempotency keys on business transactions and using our at-most-once delivery pattern in the SDK; also include server-side validation of the function payloads. We'll share example wrapper code.
[03:56] Maya Chen: Bench metrics we'll capture: tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99, cold vs warm latency (KV cache hit rate), error rate, and structural accuracy scores for JSON outputs.
[04:10] Sofia Morales: For structural outputs, we need schema enforcement. Can the platform validate outputs against a JSON schema and auto-fail if malformed?
[04:18] Liam O'Connor: We don't block on that by default, but we have server-side validators you can enable for the pilot that will flag mismatches and return a structured error. We can also attach an automated rerun job for flagged items.
[04:33] Diego Rivera: Any thoughts on quantization? We run a lot of inference at scale, if quantization reduces costs by 30% but slightly increases latency that's interesting.
[04:42] Liam O'Connor: Our runtime supports int8 and 4-bit quantized variants; we'll recommend a profile based on your sequence length distribution. The Optimize tool will suggest a target quant profile that balances quality vs cost.
[04:56] Raj Patel: Security check — SSO/SAML, RBAC, and KMS are must-haves. Also need to know if there's a private control plane for Private deployments.
[05:05] Maya Chen: Yes to SAML and RBAC. For Private we use a customer-managed control plane model with optional air-gapped installs for very regulated environments. We'll include SOC2 docs in the packet.
[05:20] Sofia Morales: Can you walk through the step-by-step benchmark we should expect? Like day 1 smoke, day 2 synthetic at 25% traffic, day 3 full replay?
[05:29] Liam O'Connor: Proposed: Day 0: sandbox integration (OpenAI-compatible). Day 1: smoke test and single-request profiling. Day 2: synthetic at 25% of peak for baseline. Day 3-4: ramp to full peak and run 4-hour sustained test. Day 5: function-calling failure injection tests and schema accuracy run. We'll produce a bench report with raw traces and summaries.
[05:52] Raj Patel: Will you provide the benchmark harness? We use JMeter + some internal drivers.
[05:57] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we'll share our harness and a JMeter plugin; we typically provide both a python load generator and a k6 script too.
[06:05] Diego Rivera: One operational concern — how are rollbacks handled during the pilot if a version introduces regressions?
[06:12] Maya Chen: Rollouts can be canaryed by route or by customer. We also support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if quality drops. For the pilot we'll set up a canary that routes 10% traffic for 24 hours then ramp.
[06:24] Sofia Morales: About cost reporting — we need token-level cost per route and alerts if cost per 1k rises above threshold.
[06:31] Maya Chen: Console shows token-level breakdowns and we can add alerting. We'll also include a cost projection based on the 7-day replay.
[06:40] Raj Patel: Let's talk about acceptance criteria again: 1) F1 >= 0.92 on structured outputs, 2) p99 latency below 450ms, 3) <1% error rate, 4) cost < $0.025 per 1k tokens. If we meet those, we move to reserved capacity procurement.
[06:58] Maya Chen: We'll codify those into the pilot SLA. Anything else from the customer side?
[07:05] Sofia Morales: Need sample SDK code that shows function-calling patterns and idempotency. Also a clear path for E2E metrics export into our Datadog.
[07:15] Liam O'Connor: We'll include example code and a Datadog ingestion guide.
[07:22] Raj Patel: Timezones for the benchmark runs — we prefer US Eastern window.
[07:26] Maya Chen: Noted.
[07:29] Diego Rivera: One more thing — do you support streaming outputs with partial structured chunks? We stream to downstream enrichment services now.
[07:36] Liam O'Connor: Streaming structured outputs is supported, but partial chunk validation is trickier. We'll recommend watermarking chunks and doing an assembly step server-side before schema validation. We'll include a proto pattern.
[07:52] Maya Chen: Ok recap: Redwood sends pilot pricing + pilot agreement, benchmark harness, SDK sample, and security pack (SOC2, KMS integration guide). Novae provides replay + success criteria doc. Schedule bench run week of 2026-12-20.
[08:05] Raj Patel: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[08:08] Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with docs and a calendar invite for the benchmark kickoff.

Notes about transcription quality: names occasionally mis-typed (e.g., "Novae" recognized as "Nova" by the auto-transcript), timestamps approximate.
